keyVerseText: I will overturn, overturn, overturn, it: and it shall be no more, until he come whose right it is; and I will give it him. I will overturn: Heb. Perverted, perverted, perverted, will I make it
rootMeaning: The root word עָוָה (ʻâvâh) conveys the idea of bending, twisting, or distorting, both in a literal and figurative sense. From this root, the noun עַוָּה (ʻavvâh) intensifies this concept to signify a state of overturning or ruin. This etymological background reveals that the word involves a fundamental disruption or perversion of what is straight or proper, going beyond a mere physical overturn to imply moral or structural distortion.
usageInScripture: The term עַוָּה appears three times in Scripture, consistently translated as 'I will overturn,' indicating an active divine judgment or disruption. Its usage emphasizes a decisive and comprehensive overthrow, often linked with ruin or distortion, underscoring the severity and totality of God's corrective action. This consistency in translation highlights the word's strong connotation of irreversible change or devastation.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עַוָּה deepens our grasp of God's sovereign authority to judge and restore order through overturning what is corrupt or perverse. The concept of distortion and ruin reflects the consequences of sin and rebellion against God's righteous standards. Yet, within this overturning lies a redemptive hope, as God's judgment paves the way for the rightful heir to receive what is due. This word reminds believers that God's justice is both just and purposeful, ultimately serving His covenantal faithfulness and the coming of Christ as the rightful King.
keyVerseReflection: Ezekiel 21:27 declares, 'I will overturn, overturn, overturn, it: and it shall be no more, until he come whose right it is; and I will give it him.' The repetition of 'overturn' (עַוָּה) intensifies the certainty and completeness of God's judgment, portraying a total perversion or destruction of the current order. This overturning is not permanent but awaits the arrival of the rightful ruler, highlighting God's sovereign plan to restore justice and rightful authority through His appointed one.
